analysis:
The change is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md gains a head-side section (about lines 956-1003) describing an engine shape-warmup stage (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The supplied units are BASE text at lines 1629-2248. They are unchanged surrounding context, and the changed hunk itself is only visible as a truncated patch excerpt. No code, config, key handling, attestation or authorization logic changes, so no threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations change.

Security-relevant claims in the visible patch text:
- Warmup uses synthetic probe prompts, not consumer data, so A-001 is not exposed.
- It trains no rate or counter.
- It runs under a 20-second wall budget; a timeout or refusal completes the attempt, and only preemption leaves it due. This bounds availability impact (T-029 and T-010 context).
- Warmup cells use the artifact's default sampling and retry at most three times. This limits resource consumption.
- Warmup interaction with prefix cache and SSD donation (T-041) is not stated in the visible text. If warmup prompts were donated to the SSD prefix cache, they would be synthetic and carry no tenant data. The implementation is not supplied, so I cannot confirm that no cache-scope or salt issue arises.

Open integration question: whether the warmup runs through the production bridge and could populate the SSD prefix cache with attacker-influenced entries. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the implementing source (ModelCalibrationPolicy, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration) is not supplied. This is recorded as an unverified contract, not a finding.

The base-text context in the units (prefix cache, MiMo native owners, Flint constraints) is pre-existing and not modified, so I report nothing from it.
